 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident caused on 08.11.2019.
02.

The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that, on 08.11.2019 at about 09.00 a.m when the petitioner was riding Scooter bearing No.KA02HW5607 on MKK Road, near Indira Canteen, a Tempo bearing No.KA02AG9019 came from behind at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.

Due to this the petitioner fell down and the said tempo (SCCH3) 3 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 ran over on her back and she was also dragged by the tempo for a distance of about 15 to 20 feet on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident she was shifted to Ananya hospital, Bengaluru and from there she was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital and admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery.
The petitioner has spent R.3,00,000/ towards her medical and other expenses.
The petitioner prior to accident was hale and healthy and was working as Doctor at Mahaveer Jain hospital and earning huge amount per month.
Even the petitioner was working as consultant in other private clinic.
Due to the accident she cannot attend to her work resulted in loss of earning and earning capacity.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the tempo driver.
Even a criminal case is registered against the said driver of tempo.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the R.C owner of the said tempo are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 had not appeared before this court on the date fixed for his appearance and hence he was placed absent throughout the proceedings.
However the respondent (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 No.1 have appeared before this Court through their counsel and filed written statement.

04. The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.1 is as under :
This respondent has issued policy in favour of respondent No.2 with respect to tempo covering the period of alleged accident.
However, the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The tempo driver did not possessed valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The accident was not occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of tempo driver, but due to the negligence of the petitioner herself.
The offending tempo has no valid permit on the date of accident.
The petitioner has not sustained loss of income and not lost earning capacity due to the accident.
This respondent has denied manner of accident, age, avocation, income and expenses incurred by the petitioner.
It is false that the petitioner due to the accident could not do any work.
The claim made by the petitioner is highly excessive.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
05. In order to prove the case, the petitioner, HR Manager and Doctors were got examined as PW.1 to 4 (SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 and got marked 34 documents as Ex.P.1 to 34 and closed her side.

2 06.
By way of rebuttal, the Legal Manager of the respondent No.1 was got examined as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed their side.

07. Heard both sides.
08.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that she has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 08.11.2019 at about 09.00 a.m on MKK Road, near Indira Canteen, 19th Main Junction,
Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the driving of the Tempo bearing registration No. KA02AG9019 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03.What Order or Award?
(SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 09.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In partly affirmative Issue No.3 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the grievance of the petitioner that she had sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the tempo bearing No.KA02AG9019.
Due to the accident she had sustained disability and put into hardship.
The same was opposed by the respondent No.1 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of driver of temp, but due to the negligence of petitioner only.
11. In order to prove this, the petitioner herself got examined as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in her affidavit.
In her cross examination she has admitted that "I have done MBBS, DGO, DNB.
I was working with Bhagwan Mahaveer hospital since 2007.
As on today I do not have any source of income.
I was paid Rs.1,02,000/ per month by Mahaveer Jain hospital.
Other than this I had (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 earning from other source where I was visiting doctor.
Now I am not doing the work of consultancy.
It is true that I have not surrendered my licence at KMC.
On the date of accident I was proceeding on two wheeler and hit by tempo from behind.
For spinal chord rod and screws are inserted.
At the Mahaveer Jain hospital some medical bills expenses are reimbursed.
I have not engaged any person for attendent but every day some one will help.
I was not running a clinic ".
The PW.1 had denied her negligence for the accident and other suggestions of the respondent No.1 counsel.
12. Per contra, the Legal Manager of the respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in his affidavit.

The RW.1 has got marked Dr.S.Srividya vs Reliance General Insurance on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94405345/
3
Authorization letter and copy of Policy as per Ex.R.1 and 2.
So as per Ex.R.2 the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
13. The RW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "It is true that we have not produced any document to show that our insured vehicle has no valid FC as on the date of accident.
It is true that the police have filed chargesheet against the tempo driver bearing registration No.KA02AG 9019, but it is wrong".
(SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 14. The PW.1 in support of the case had got marked entire police records as per Ex.P.1 to 5.

On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation has filed Charge sheet against tempo driver for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of IPC and U/s 56 and 192 of IMV Act.
Further the I.O has stated that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of tempo driver only.

The I.O has also stated that as on the date of accident the said tempo was not having valid F.C.
15.
The respondent No.1 contend that the accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner herself.
Hence they are not liable to pay compensation.

In order to prove their contention eventhough the RW.1 was got examined but there are no supportive oral and documentary evidence in this regard.
16.
Even the petitioner has marked mahazar and sketch as per Ex.P.2 and 3 and on perusal of these documents it is true that the accident occurred on MKK Road, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru.
Even there are no documents on behalf of the respondent No.1 to show that the accident occurred due to the negligence of petitioner herself.
The respondent No.1 have not (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 proved that petitioner too contributed for the accident.
Without challenging the chargesheet and not producing any cogent documents the respondent No.1 cannot contend that the concerned I.O have filed wrong chargesheet.

Hence with the available documents on record and in absence of rebuttal evidence by the respondents, I am of opinion that the petitioner has proved that she had sustained injuries only due to the rash and negligent of tempo driver only.
Even the respondent No.2 has not whispered anything in this regard.
Hence I answered issue No.1 in affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:
Further the petitioner has stated that due to the accident she is not able to do her earlier work and lost income.
In this regard she has got examined the HR Manager as PW.2 who had stated that the petitioner was appointed as Consultant in Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital with effect from 01.09.2014.
The petitioner was paid Rs.1,02,007/ as salary.
The petitioner was on earned leave till 13.12.2019.
The petitioner had not attend to her job since 08.11.2019 till 14.02.2022 and she was not paid salary from 14.12.2019 to 14.02.2022.
That on (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 14.02.2022 the petitioner had tendered resignation which was accepted by the hospital.

18. The PW.2 had got marked the Pay slip, Attendence sheet, Joining report, Office letter,
Resignation acceptance letter and Service letter as per Ex.P.22 to 31.

So on perusal of these Dr.S.Srividya vs Reliance General Insurance on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94405345/
4 documents it is clear that prior to the accident the petitioner was working as Junior Consultant and after the accident she was resigned to the said job.
It is not coming forth before this court as to whether the petitioner had voluntarily resigned the job or the hospital authorities have made the petitioner to resign from the job.
19. The PW.2 in his cross examination has admitted that "At the time of accident the petitioner was working as junior consultant.
There is no incentive for the petitioner.
There is no group or personal insurance for the petitioner.
The petitioner herself resigned from the job.

At the time of accident the petitioner was paid with gross salary of Rs.1,02,007/ and the deduction is of Rs.11,151/".
20.
At this stage the petitioner had relied upon decisions reported in a. 2022 ACJ 2048 - Jagadeesh Suvarna V/s K.T.Rajashekar and another -

sentences.text: It is observed that when (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 injured lost sensation of both legs and bedridden then attendant charges would be awarded.
b. Civil appeal No.2205/2022 - Master Ayush Vs Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that looking into the physical condition of the injured attendent charges would be awarded.

c. MFA.No.6105/2019 (MV) - Lokeshaiah Vs Lakshmegowda and another - It is observed that when the injured was in paraplegia condition the pain and agony could not be ascertained and hence attendent charges to be awarded.
21. But in the present case the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that she had appointed an attendent and incurred amount to pay them.
Even the PW.1 in her cross examination has admitted that she had not appointed an attendent but daily some body will come and help.
22. The petitioner had got marked the salary slip for the month of December 2019 and payment summary as per Ex.P.22 and 23.
So as per Ex.P.22 and 23 it is true that the petitioner was getting Rs.1,02,007/ per month as salary.
Hence there is no other ground to disbelieve this salary for the petitioner.
Hence the monthly salary for the petitioner as on the date of accident would be Rs.1,02,007/.
( SCCH3
. The petitioner also examined Spine Surgeon as PW.3 who had stated that the petitioner had sustained injuries to neck, chest and left upper limb.
The petitioner complains of pins and needle sensation over the bilateral lower limb, unable to walk, stand.
The petitioner was admitted for physiotherapy and rehabilitation.
The petitioner had underwent surgeries also.

The PW.3 had got marked inpatient records as per Ex.P.32.
24.
The PW.3 in his cross examination has admitted that "That I am one of the treated doctor.
That as per the recent examination there was no improvement on D3 compression.
It is true that I am not aware about the recent position of paraplegia condition.
At this stage the situation is uncertain that the petitioner may or may not recover.

The insertion of rod and screw to the petitioner are usually Dr.S.Srividya vs Reliance General Insurance on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94405345/
5 permanent.
The nerve system of the petitioner was damaged as the nerve system of D5 is damaged.

The petitioner is not having sensation below D5 level".
25.

Further the petitioner in support of her case has got examined Senior Consultant as PW.4 who had stated that on clinical examination it is noticed that the petitioner has lost sensation, movement and (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 strength in both hip regions in both lower limbs.
The surgical scar are present.
The petitioner may have difficulty lying on back or to sleep on the back for long hours due to presence of multiple implants.
The petitioner cannot do physical work daily and needs assistance.
The bladder sensation is absent due to loss of strength in both hip regions and both lower limb.
26. The PW.4 has assessed the permanent residual physical disability of 95% to whole body.

Even the PW.4 had got marked Outpatient record and Xray as per Ex.P.33 and 34.
27.
The PW.4 in his cross examination has admitted that "It is true that there is no loss of intellectual memory and intellectual knowledge.
It is true that the petitioner now is on wheel chair.
It is true that the procedure was done for only D1 to D4.
It is true that no plate was fixed for D1 to D4, but only screw and rod were fixed.
It is true that the said rod and screw are permanent.
The decompression will remain as usual and there will be no changes.
That there will be natural gap in between D1 to D3.
It is true that there will not abnormal gaps in between D1 to D3.
Now the petitioner is under paraplegia status.
It is true that now the cord edema is normal.
That now the nerve (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 system is irreversible.

It is true that apart from vertebra and spinal cord injury there are no other injuries".
28.
The PW.4 had assessed 95% of whole body disability.
But he had not divided into 1/3rd which comes to 31%.
Hence, from the oral evidence of PW.1 to 4 and as per the documents produced it is true that the petitioner has sustained disability due to the accident, but not as stated by the PW.4.

Even looking into the age of the injured, nature of treatment obtained and the medical records, I just feel it proper to consider 28% disability for the petitioner.
29.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
a). Loss of future income:
The PW.1 has stated that she was working as Junior consultant and as per the above finding it is true that the petitioner as on the date of accident was getting Rs.1,02,007/ per month.
Further the petitioner has stated that she was aged about 44 years at the time of accident.
In this regard the PW.1 has got marked her Aadhaar card and Driving licence as per Ex.P.16 and 17 which reveals that the PW.1 was born in the year 1975.
Hence as per (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 the said document it is just and proper to consider the age of the petitioner as 44 years at the time of accident.
Thereby proper multiplier comes to "14".
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income as Rs.1,02,007 x 12 x 14 x 28/100 = Rs.47,98,409/ under this head.

6 b).

sentences.text: Pain and sufferings during treatment period: The petitioner has stated that she was admitted in hospital as inpatient.
In this regard she had got marked the discharge summary as per Ex.P.8 and 9 which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient from 08.11.2019 to 20.11.2019 and from 02.01.2020 to 08.01.2020.
Hence under these circumstances, I just feel it proper to award Rs.30,000/ under this head.
c). Towards medical expenses:
The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.10 which amounts to Rs.31,082/. Further the PW.1 has got marked other bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.72,031/.
It is true that there are no other corroborative documents to prove the Ex.P.11.
But it is also true that the petitioner had obtained the treatment as per Ex.P.11 and she had paid the said (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 amount.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,03,113/ under this head.

d). Loss of income during laid up period:-
Admittedly the PW.1 as per available records could not do any work for about one month.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,000/ under this head.

e). Loss of amenities and nutrition food:-
The PW.1 had not produced any documents to show that she had incurred amount towards amenities and nutritious food.
But looking into the period of treatment and the nature of injuries, I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.
f). Towards attendent charges and conveyance:
The PW.1 was admitted as inpatient for nearly 18 days.
In these days the petitioner has to look after by some body.
Hence under these circumstances I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
g). Towards future medical expenses:
The PW.4 has stated that petitioner needs further follow up treatment and physiotherapy sessions.
In this regard there is no supportive documents.
Hence under these (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 circumstances I just feel it proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/ under this head.
30. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.50,39,522/ (Fifty lakhs thirty nine thousand five thousand and twenty two only).
31. Regarding liability: The respondent No.21 has admitted the issuance of policy in the name of the respondent No.2.
It is true that the petitioner has proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending tempo driver.
The said offending tempo was owned by the respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.1.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answered the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.

7 32.
Issue No.3:

Further as per my above findings on above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioner is entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,39,522/ (Fifty lakhs thirty nine thousand five thousand and twenty two only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a (the interest awarded is not applicable to future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of valid insurance policy, respondent No.1  Insurance Company is directed to pay the total awarded amount and shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or schedule bank of her choice for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to her through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
(SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.7724/2019
However, PW.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, got typed by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in open court, on this the 19th day of April 2023).

As such I proceed to pass the following: (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.7724/2019 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,39,522/ (Fifty lakhs thirty nine thousand five thousand and twenty two only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a (the interest awarded is not applicable to future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, in view of valid insurance policy, respondent No.1  Insurance Company is directed to pay the total awarded amount and shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest accrued, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or schedule bank of her choice for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to her through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
(SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.7724/2019
However, PW.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
